key_insight: The paper tackles cross-process weld penetration prediction by making a model trained on one welding process adapt to another without target labels. Its core idea is to use unsupervised domain adaptation plus gradual source domain expansion to reduce the performance drop caused by very different welding physics.
problem_solved: Supervised weld penetration classifiers often fail when transferred across welding processes like TIG and laser welding because the data distributions and physical mechanisms differ significantly. This work addresses the domain shift problem in cross-process welding state prediction.
method: Build an unsupervised domain adaptation framework to transfer knowledge from a labeled source welding process to an unlabeled target process.
Incorporate gradual source domain expansion (GSDE) to progressively widen the source data coverage and improve alignment with the target domain.
Learn domain-invariant features so the model can predict penetration status reliably across different welding mechanisms.
impact: This approach helps AI practitioners deploy weld inspection models in real manufacturing settings where labeled target data is scarce or unavailable. It also demonstrates a practical strategy for transferring deep learning across strongly shifted industrial domains.
